86: ✦This week your baby's face is still small in proportion to the body.✦They look cuter with each passing day.✦The facial features have become more defined.✦The forehead is broad.✦As the ears grow, they take on their normal shape.✦The inner and middle ear have fully formed.✦The eyes have moved further toward the front of the face.✦The eyes have gained colour.
87: ✦The baby's skin is covered with fine hair.✦Your baby can put their thumb in their mouth.✦By this week all of your baby's organs and body systems have formed.✦The organs keep growing and developing, and the arms and legs keep getting longer.
88: ✦The baby's digestive system is working well.✦The baby swallows amniotic fluid, filters it through the kidneys and intestines and releases it back into the amniotic fluid as urine.✦All waste is passed through the umbilical cord to the placenta and from there into the mother's blood.
89: ✦All of your baby's tooth buds keep developing.✦Your baby can now stretch the whole body and respond to outside stimuli with reflex movements.✦Babies don't feel any pain from these stimuli.
90: ✦The heart is a little slower than in previous weeks, but still beats fast.✦The yolk sac disappears completely this week.✦The intestines are now fully settled inside the abdomen.
91: ✦Your baby's head is half the length of the body, but the body will catch up in the coming weeks.✦The developing organs have started working.✦The liver secretes bile, the pancreas produces insulin and the kidneys make urine.✦The vocal cords have also started to develop as your baby prepares to communicate after birth.
92: ✦This week your baby is 8–9 cm long, about the size of a medium apple.✦It weighs about 43–45 grams.
93: ✦In boys the prostate is forming; in girls the ovaries are moving down toward the pelvis.✦This week lanugo – temporary fine hair that falls out within a few weeks after birth – has appeared on the skin.✦It's thought to keep the baby warm until enough fat builds up under the skin.
94: ✦This week the baby's brain keeps developing.✦The connections between brain, nerves and muscles are nearly complete.✦As nerve fibres are now covered with a fatty myelin layer, messages from the brain start reaching organs and muscles.✦This shows in the facial muscles too.✦Over the past weeks the baby started making various (uncontrolled) facial expressions; this week they go further – frowning or making a sour face.
95: ✦This week the placenta keeps growing and producing hormones for the baby's development.✦Until birth it provides the nutrients and oxygen the baby needs.✦The placenta also works as a filter.✦It helps reduce the effect of some factors, such as medicines the mother has to take.
96: ✦An ever-growing uterus.✦At each prenatal visit your provider will note the size of your uterus by measuring from your pubic bone to the top of the uterus (fundus).✦In general this measurement matches the week of pregnancy you're in.
97: ✦On ultrasound this week your baby still looks roomy and comfortable.✦In the images the baby's head is often on the right with a hand near the chest.
98: ✦There are only a few weeks left until you can learn your baby's sex.✦Your doctor might see it this week or give you a hint.✦Since a guess could be wrong, you can ask your doctor not to tell you anything yet if they're not sure.
99: ✦Your baby is 10–11 cm long, about the size of a medium peach.✦It weighs about 70 grams.
100: ✦Your baby's eyes are still tightly closed and won't open until about week 23.✦But they can now notice bright light coming through your belly and hear sounds.
101: ✦The thyroid hormones have been working for a few weeks.✦Last week a fatty layer called myelin began forming around the nerves connecting the muscles to the brain.
102: ✦Your baby can move the arms and legs at the joints much faster and turn the head from side to side. Active enough to somersault, punch and kick, your baby practically does acrobatics in your belly. The umbilical cord, made of 3 blood vessels, gives the flexibility for these movements. Your baby can suck their fingers.
103: ✦The baby still makes involuntary facial expressions.✦By making faces like surprise, sadness, anger and smiles, the baby is stretching and exercising the facial muscles.
104: ✦There is still little fat under the skin.✦The baby's fine hair called lanugo has grown.✦Most of it falls out before birth and some after; it's thought to keep the baby warm until fat builds up in the skin.
105: ✦Your baby's skin is still very thin.✦If you could look inside, you'd see the ribs and blood vessels under the skin.✦Babies are quite active now and use their waking time to move and stretch their muscles.✦Your baby may even have started sucking their thumb.
106: ✦This week your baby is excitedly moving their arms and legs.✦Sometime between this week and week twenty, you may feel movement for the first time.✦Still, your baby is very small – about 11.5 to 12 cm and around 85 grams – and the cushion of amniotic fluid makes movements hard to feel at this point.
107: ✦As you've probably noticed, sleeping on your stomach is almost impossible by now.✦Lying on your back is thought to put pressure on the main vein returning blood to your heart, so lying on your left side is best.✦Sleeping in this position improves circulation and minimises the chance of swelling (oedema) and varicose veins.
108: ✦Your baby keeps making facial expressions like surprise, sadness, frowning and smiling.✦Don't worry – these aren't real emotional reactions; they're involuntary.✦Think of them as practice and exercises for the facial muscles.
109: ✦Your baby can make grasping movements with their hands.✦They can even clasp their hands together or hold the umbilical cord.✦The hair is starting to get thicker.
110: ✦At 16 weeks your baby keeps swallowing amniotic fluid and passing it through the digestive system as urine.✦In baby girls, hundreds of thousands of eggs form in the ovaries this week.✦The baby can kick with those tiny feet.
111: ✦The eyes become more sensitive to light.✦The ears have started to hear.✦The placenta, which completed its development around weeks 12–13, lets the baby breathe, feed and get rid of waste.✦It also protects the baby from infections.✦It works very fast and uses a lot of energy, like an organ.✦That's why it receives a large blood supply.✦As the fetus grows and needs more, the placenta will thicken.✦The placenta is now about 1 cm thick and about 7–8 cm across.
112: ✦On ultrasound your doctor can see your baby's body structures; organs such as the heart, diaphragm and kidneys can be observed.✦Your doctor can also check blood flow in the placenta and umbilical cord.
113: ✦The hair, eyebrows and eyelashes are growing.✦The baby can open and close their mouth.✦They can move their closed eyes.✦Your baby is gaining weight along with you, but doesn't have enough fat yet because the fat-storing tissue has only just started to form.
114: ✦All the major systems inside your baby are almost complete. The heart can beat 140–150 times a minute.✦The respiratory system is developing too; the chest is making breathing movements.
115: ✦Feeling your baby grow inside you must be one of the most beautiful feelings in the world.✦At the same time you're probably curious about what's happening in there and how your baby is developing.
116: ✦The baby's arms, legs, head and body are now in proportion.✦The skin keeps changing; fat is starting to build up and sweat glands are developing.✦This fat protects the baby.✦It also produces body heat, keeping the baby warm.✦As fat builds up, your baby will become chubbier before birth.
117: ✦This week the baby starts storing calcium.✦So it's good to keep eating calcium-rich foods.✦The baby's heartbeat has started to be regulated by the brain.
118: ✦The placenta keeps growing with your baby, managing the exchange between mother and baby and filtering out carbon dioxide.✦The baby can hear sounds and sense bright light through your belly.
119: ✦Everything is fine in the body systems and they're working well.✦The digestive system is always working because the baby swallows amniotic fluid and urinates.✦Meanwhile, the baby keeps practising breathing.
120: ✦Your baby can now hear much better, so communicating with them becomes even more enjoyable.✦Talk and sing to your baby whenever you can – they can hear both you and your partner.✦If you gently push on your belly while talking, they'll feel you.✦You can also play classical music.✦The more you communicate, the better your baby will recognise your voice in the coming weeks.✦They can hear your heartbeat and the sounds of your organs.✦Their own heart rate may change in response to outside sounds.✦If you go to a lively concert, your baby may make fast, jumping movements.
121: ✦Your baby's sex organs have developed.✦In baby girls millions of eggs have formed.✦By birth this number drops to 1–2 million.✦The uterus and vaginal canal have started to form.✦In baby boys, development of the prostate is completed this week.✦The testicles haven't yet descended from the abdomen into the scrotum.✦In both boys and girls, the mammary glands and nipples have developed.
122: ✦Stool called meconium starts to form in the intestines.✦As breathing practice speeds up, the sucking and swallowing reflexes develop too.✦Your baby can swallow amniotic fluid.✦Because the baby passes it as urine, the amniotic fluid is constantly renewed.✦With enough amniotic fluid, the lungs develop healthily.✦Although babies get oxygen and nutrients from the placenta until birth, the lungs must expand and contract in amniotic fluid to prepare for breathing after birth.
123: ✦The ability to grasp keeps developing.✦With those tiny, thin fingers your baby can hold their face or the umbilical cord.✦Your baby may yawn when sleepy.✦You may feel hiccups as little rhythmic jumps.✦Even with closed eyes, the baby can move them left and right.✦Babies can sleep for 20 minutes to 2 hours at a time in the womb.
124: ✦You can see your baby's arm and leg movements.✦The baby may be seen opening and closing the mouth.✦On ultrasound they may stick out their tongue.
125: ✦Your baby is about 14 cm long and keeps growing quickly.✦They now have a daily routine and sleep habits.✦If it's a boy, the genitals can easily be seen on ultrasound.✦If you're having a girl, the uterus and fallopian tubes have formed and settled into place.
126: ✦Unique fingerprints are beginning to form and the grip is getting stronger.✦The ears are working and can react to loud noises from outside.✦These reactions may come as kicks.✦But if this is your first pregnancy, you may not notice these soft sensations yet.
127: ✦Air sacs are developing in the tiny lungs.✦Your baby may already have hiccups, but you can't feel them yet.
128: ✦Your baby is 16–18 cm long, about the size of a small melon.✦It weighs about 240–250 grams.
129: ✦Something important is about to happen: a layer called vernix will start to form on the baby's skin.✦This layer is thickest in the last 3 months.✦Some of it is still on the body when the baby is born.✦It protects the baby's skin from the acidity of the amniotic fluid.✦It also helps the baby slide through the birth canal during delivery.
130: ✦The baby's whole body, including the eyelids and upper lip, is covered with a fine layer of hair (lanugo).
131: ✦As muscle development continues, the baby gets stronger.✦Since starting to move the arms weeks ago, the baby can now throw quicker punches and kicks.✦The fat under the baby's skin keeps thickening.✦This fat helps maintain body temperature.✦It also keeps the baby warm after birth.
132: ✦The baby's nervous system keeps building connections between the brain and every part of the body.✦This supports rapid development of the senses.✦At 19 weeks your baby can hear sounds very well.✦They can hear the sounds inside you, especially your heartbeat and the sounds of your stomach and intestines.✦They may react to loud outside noises with a jumpy movement.✦The sense of taste also starts to develop this week.✦Your baby can taste the amniotic fluid.
133: ✦Your baby's sex organs have developed.✦In baby girls about 6 million eggs have formed this week.✦By birth this number drops to 1–2 million.✦The uterus and vaginal canal of a baby girl develop this week.✦In baby boys, the prostate finished developing last week.✦The testicles haven't yet descended from the abdomen into the scrotum.
134: ✦On ultrasound your uterus may appear a little low.✦Don't worry – the uterus grows both up and down during pregnancy.✦The placenta, however, is not expected to be low this week.
135: ✦Your baby continues to mature.✦The nails and eyebrows have started to appear.✦The hair that began growing earlier keeps growing.✦The baby keeps swallowing and practising breathing.✦The baby can open and close their mouth regularly.✦They can stick out their tongue.
